preview: Interview experience of Jash Shah for the Graduate Analyst role at Deutsche Bank in 2023, detailing the online coding round, two technical rounds, a professional fitness round, and an HR round.
content: Interview Experience Deutsche Bank Jash Shah - Graduate Analyst Final Year, BTech Computer Engineering 2020-24 09th August 2023. Introduction Companies for campus placements in 2023 were sparse since there was a recession in the tech job market. None of the big 4 companies ( Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, SAP Labs) that normally visited our college participated in the campus hiring process. Deutsche Bank visited our campus in the first week of August to hire final-year students for the role of Graduate Analyst in the Technology, Data and Innovation (TDI) division. CTC: 19.63LPA Job Description: Our technology teams deliver and manage engineering solutions to support the bank’s global customers. You will develop and deliver solutions to help modernise technology solutions, reduce complexity and risk, and to drive business growth. You will be part of a creative, collaborative, and innovative team, partnering with others, and sharing solutions and you will have a strong desire to make an impact. We offer a structured entry-level rotational programme that will equip you with the foundational knowledge and skills necessary to build a long-term career as a technology professional at Deutsche Bank. Depending on your rotation you will gain expertise in: • Designing & delivering engineering solutions for our businesses and customers • Providing production engineering services to ensure the safety and reliability of our technology • Analyzing business data within DB to inform plans and deliveries • Enhancing our infrastructure capabilities and functions • Using standard design patterns for strategic DB frameworks like Fabric, Autobahn, and GLUE. CPI: 7 and above Branches Eligible: Computers, IT & EXTC (Electronics and Telecommunication). Online Coding Round 1.5hrs - 4th August 2023 3 coding questions Question-wise difficulty: Easy - Medium - Medium Question-wise scoring: 20 - 50 - 50 Partial marking was present if you are only able to clear some test cases 1. Given two resources with powers A and B respectively. At each second, you have to select one resource out of the two to run the software, The power of the resource at the time of selection should be greater than 1. Every second, the power of the selected resource gets reduced by 2 and the power of the unselected resource gets charged by 1. The software stops when at least one resource has a power of 0. 2. Given a dictionary of N words and a query word S, you need to auto-suggest the best word from the dictionary that is closest to S. Two words are first compared by their Levenshtein distance to the word S. If two words have the same Levenshtein distance, then the lexicographically smaller word is given the priority. All words, along with S, are lowercase. 3. Backlinks are links from other websites to a particular web resource, and they play a crucial role in the SEO of pages. You are given N webpage titles and corresponding arrays that constrain the number of backlinks for each webpage. The objective is to rank the web pages in descending order based on the number of backlinks they have. If two or more pages have the same number of links then maintain their ordering. I was able to solve all the test cases of all three problems and got selected for the interviews. Many of my friends were also able to solve all the test cases for all three problems, some in even lesser time than me, but were not selected. The selection criteria for the coding round are still a mystery to most students. I would suggest, having a good CPI, a good resume and a fairly good time of submission can go a long way in passing the first round. There is a lot of luck and chance involved in who gets to pass the Coding round of all companies. So don’t get discouraged, if you are not selected despite having the best-case solution in the least time. Technical Interview - 1 45 mins - 11.30 AM, 09th August 2023 The interviews started at 9:00 AM and my first interview came at 11:30 AM ( I was one of the last ones to get called ). There was a single female interviewer, and the round lasted around 45 mins. 1. Introduce Yourself 2. Which language are you most comfortable with? I answered with Python, as most of the projects in my resume revolved around Python. I also mentioned being comfortable in C and C++ This came with a follow-up question on why Python and not Java/C++? I answered by listing the accessibility, wider community and easier interpretability of Python as the reasons. Another follow-up question was how to implement OOPs in Python? I mentioned my internship at DE Shaw and GSoC where I used multiple OOPs concepts such as inheritance and encapsulation in my projects there A follow-up question was to explain the different types of Inheritance? Tip: Always guide the interview back to the projects you’ve done. And give examples from your work. This adds a lot more credibility to your answers. Another follow up question, was how to perform exception handling in Python? Again, I mentioned creating custom Exception Classes during my GSoC internship and how that feeds into the previous question of how OOP is used to derive all these custom Error classes in Python from a Base Exception class. 3. What is your favourite Data Structure? I jokingly answered by saying, that it changes based on the current project I’m working on. But I mentioned graphs and linear structures being the current ones I’m most comfortable with since I had worked on Graphs extensively during my corporate internship. The follow up question to this was to write a code in Python to detect loops in Linked List. I knew the optimal solution but I started with the naive approach and derived Floyds Cycle Finding Algorithm 4. Torch and Bridge Puzzle I gave a solution which wasn’t the best. She asked me multiple times to confirm if I thought it was the best possible solution. I couldnt think come up with a better solution. It wasn’t a coding problem but I managed to came up with a DP solution, which I proved would always give the best solution. She was impressed by this approach. 5. Merge Sort vs Quick Sort I mentioned that Quick Sort is unstable while Merge Sort is stable. A follow-up question was to prove this, which I did by taking an example with duplicate elements and dry run both algorithms.. I couldn’t come up with any more examples, even though I had read about them. Tip: When learning, try to understand with examples and dry-running atleast one example for each concept. This way even if you can’t remember the exact property of a data structure or algorithm ( which is very common ), you can derive it. 6. Are you comfortable with DBMS? I answered by saying not too much since I hadn’t worked hands-on with any yet. So she asked me basic questions What are ACID properties? 7. Are you comfortable with Computer Network concepts? Again, I answered by saying that I know the theory but don’t have practical experience. TCP vs UDP I explained the connection-oriented vs connectionless, and reliability as the major differences. I went onto explain the SYN-ACK and Request-Response protocols for both. 8. Are you comfortable with OS concepts? I answered with yes, since I had some experience working with them. Also, I was confident about my theoretical knowledge in them. Explain Virtual Memory 9. Finally I was asked to elaborate on the project I worked on as part of E-Yantra Robotics Competition, which is something I’m very comfortable talking about. 10. Any questions you have for me? I asked what their day-to-day at Deutsche is like, and the techstack they work in. Out of 41 students, 35 were shortlisted for the second technical round. Technical Interview - 2 30 mins - 1:00 PM, 09th August, 2023 The second round started post lunch, and my second interview came pretty early this time, at around 1:00 PM. There was a single female interviewer and the round lasted around 30 mins. 1. Introduction 2. Why do you want to work in Deutsche Bank over DE Shaw? This was a very common question to most students. The answer might vary depending on you. I answered with the concern of WLB and Deutsche Bank being a 150+ year old company making it a more secure job. A follow-up question was, how I could be sure that the WLB at Deutsche wasn’t just as bad or worse than DE Shaw? I answered by saying that I had heard the experiences of my trusted friends who had interned there and I was using that as the basis of my choice. 3. What is your response to being asked to work on weekends? I answered by saying that, if the requirement was critical and the firm provides adequate compensation and appreciation, then I would be willing to do it on some occasions. She smirked, and seemed satisfied with the response. 4. Distance covered by Bee puzzle 5. Which is the concept related to code reusabality in OOP? I was thinking out loud and mentioned encapsulation, which the interviewer thought was my final answer, and so she corrected me saying inheritance was the correct answer. 6. SQL query to remove duplicate elements from a table I gave the concept of the solution in the link above, but wasnt able to write the query perfectly ( SQL has always been my weakness ). She asked me to give another approach, to which I mentioned using self-join, because I had read this solution. But I again couldnt give the perfect query. Tip: If you don’t know the answer to any question perfectly, then mention that but still take a stab at it. The interviewer wants to test your problem solving skills and not your memory, so try to be confident and coming up with the best possible, most reasonable answer you can on the spot. 7. Swapping two nos. without using a third variable. This was a very easy question, but on the spot I couldnt answer it. I gave the solution in Python: x, y = y, x 8. What would you do in case of disagreements in your team regarding an idea you proposed? I answered saying, that its not about imposing my own idea but coming to the most optimal compromise. Considering that everyone in the team is reasonable, the burden of proof falls on me to put forth the best possible arguments for my idea. 9. Any question for the interviewer? I asked her experience at Deutsche and her thoughts on their WLB. The second round was fairly shorter, but I felt I messed up more than I should’ve. Out of 35 students, 26 were selected for the next round. Professional Fitness Round 25 mins - 4:00 PM, 09th August, 2023 The Professional Fitness round is to basically test if you are the right fit for the firm and match their mottos. It’s good practice to read up a bit about the goals and verticals of the firm. There was a single male interviewer and the round lasted about 25 mins. It was much more relaxed and less hostile than the Technical Rounds. 1. No Intro this time luckily ;) 2. Glass half full puzzle 3. Cut cake into 8 equal pieces with 3 strokes puzzle I wasnt able to answer either of these puzzles, but I was thinking out loud and tried to make by thought process very clear 4. A very in-depth explanation of the Architecture diagram on two projects from my resume. This was an unexpected question in the Profit round, and the interviewer seemed to be very interested in my E-Yantra Project and how we went about solving the tasks in that competition. Tip: Be very thorough with ever single line on your resume, your work in the projects you’ve done and the challenges/learnings of each of them. Since, I mentioned using Lua as the programming language in my E-Yantra project, he asked Why lua was used over CPP? 5. Any questions for me? I asked him about the Pune office and what was the idealogoy of Deutsche about WFH. Out of 26 shortlisted for Profit, all were asked to give the HR round as well. HR Round 20 mins - 7:00 PM, 09th August 2023 Everyone selected for the ProFit round was also asked to give the HR round. 1. Introduction. 2. What do you excel at aside from studies? I mentioned gaming, table tennis, swimming 3. Why Deutsche Bank? I again answered with the same point of security and being close to home. A follow-up question was: What if we ask you to relocate permanently to somewhere far? I answered by saying, that with the right compensation and relocation assistance and weighing the pros and cons at that time. 4. Any questions for me? What activities do you organize as an HR to ensure WLB? What is the idealogy behid lateral transfers? Out of 41 students in total, 26 were selected for the ProFit and Final HR round, and all 26 were selected for the PPO. FAQs How to prepare an Intro? Start by mentioning your branch, year and field of study. Then move through your experiences and MAJOR projects only one by one. If you move through them chronologically, you can build up a rough “storyline” on why you decided to do certain projects at a certain time. End the intro, with a brief summary of how your journey till now has shaped you, what you are passionate about currently, and how the role you are applying for falls in line with that goal. Keep it under 2 mins. For technical rounds, think of it as giving the interviewer a high-level tour of the experiences and projects in your resume. For HR rounds, think of it as informing the interviewer of the learnings and challenges your face in the experiences, achievements and PORs in your resume. Resources System Design, DBMS, OS, CN.
